# Documents

Each document under docs/ says in its front matter what it is (tools/docs.py). Superseded ones
are left out here; each names what replaced it. docs/upstream/ holds others' text, as fetched.

## Current

How blaze is now. Kept true: CI checks their links, paths and settings against the tree.

- [benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md): How long an edit takes to build, the memory and disk it uses and how fast its programs run, against cargo, on three platforms.
- [borrowck.md](borrowck.md): blaze's own borrow checker (hir-ty-borrowck): how it matches rustc's verdicts, how it is scored, what is left.
- [cargo.md](cargo.md): Every blaze command and setting: cargo's commands and flags, what a build does, sandboxing, manifests.
- [const.md](const.md): Const evaluation: blaze's own interpreter for constants and const fns, and what it covers.
- [contributing.md](contributing.md): How to build, test and change blaze: AI use, where new code goes, rules for code, working in parallel, landing.
- [fuzzing.md](fuzzing.md): The fuzzers: generated programs and edits, each held to blaze's own build from nothing (a warm daemon, a warm store), what a finding is, and what they do not cover.
- [gc.md](gc.md): What blaze removes from disk and when: the collector of build dirs, shared std stores, temporaries and trash; the pacer that works harder as a volume fills, leases, records, roots and the grace, and why nothing in use is removed.
- [harness.md](harness.md): The harnesses that test blaze (real crates' own tests, and blaze held to itself), what each checks, and how CI runs them.
- [install.md](install.md): Installing blaze: the install script, the release channels and what gets installed.
- [ix-prof.md](ix-prof.md): Profiling any Rust program, not only blaze, like Go's pprof. Covers the ix-prof crate (CPU samples of every thread, tracing spans with their own CPU time and allocations, named waits, allocations by stack), `IX_PROF=<dir>`, the loopback `/debug/pprof` endpoint and live stream, and `blaze pprof` with top, peek, tree, list, flame, diff, export and --http.
- [lints.md](lints.md): The general `blaze::` lints `blaze check` runs in every workspace (`blaze::general`): what each catches, why it costs, how to fix or allow it, and the `clippy.toml` keys that tune them.
- [mir-passes.md](mir-passes.md): The MIR passes from built MIR to runtime MIR, ported from rustc, that codegen and the interpreter run on.
- [release.md](release.md): Releases: the canary and stable channels, how a release is cut and what gates promotion to stable.
- [resolve.md](resolve.md): Reading Cargo.toml and .cargo/config.toml as cargo does (blaze-manifest), and how it measured against cargo.
- [toolchain.md](toolchain.md): blaze's own pinned nightly: what it is, how it is fetched and checked, and the daily bump.
- [usage.md](usage.md): Getting started: using blaze on a project, in short.
- [v2/plan/invariants.md](v2/plan/invariants.md): Every invariant, refinement and reference model blaze states in its code, with the test that checks it and the planted bugs that prove the check; generated by harness/v2/invariants.py.
- [v2/plan/design/profile-names.md](v2/plan/design/profile-names.md): The flight recorder names strings per thread. Each thread interns into a private table whose ids are scoped to its own ring, defines each name in the ring the first time it uses it, and starts a new generation at chunk boundaries. Readers turn per-thread ids into global ones as they decode, so the hot path shares nothing and the profile parquet is unchanged.

## Plans

Designs not (fully) built, newest first.

- [v2/plan/objectives.md](v2/plan/objectives.md) (2026-11-09): The ledger. Every objective of the plan, the check that decides it and where it stands; generated from objectives.json by harness/v2/ledger.py.
- [v2/plan/design/tasks.md](v2/plan/design/tasks.md) (2026-11-09): Tasks in the agent app. Every agent belongs to a task, the sidebar lists tasks with their agents under them, and a task says what it waits on, what it costs and how it ended.
- [v2/plan/design/store-pool.md](v2/plan/design/store-pool.md) (2026-11-09): The store's hot tier as a vmcache-style buffer pool - one reserved range with a fixed slot per page of every store file, a state word per page (optimistic and pinned reads), misses as explicit reads through blaze-core that the task yields on, immutable records written once through the pool, eviction by the one evictor with MADV_DONTNEED / MADV_FREE_REUSABLE, prefetch we plan ourselves (change set, query graph, learned page sets, per-view warm sets), codegen outputs then memos then the image on it, a DST, and the lanes.
- [v2/plan/design/std.md](v2/plan/design/std.md) (2026-11-09): blaze's own standard library, written from scratch on core and alloc. No ambient authority (main receives an Io and every function touches only what it is handed), sans-IO underneath (one Io over io_uring, kqueue, IOCP and the simulation), and every blaze crate moves onto it.
- [v2/plan/design/edition.md](v2/plan/design/edition.md) (2026-11-09): The blaze edition. Rust with ten opt-in changes (handles that copy themselves, error unions, view types, records, contexts, effects at the border, values that must be used up, contracts and pattern types, compile-time reflection, `&uniq`), what it removes, the lints that get a crate ready for it, and the order it is built in.
- [v2/plan/design/comptime.md](v2/plan/design/comptime.md) (2026-11-09): Compile-time reflection in blaze. Phase 1 completes nightly `core::mem::type_info` in blaze's const evaluator; phase 2 is the opt-in `blaze_comptime` extension (`for const f in fields_of::<T>()`, `self.[f]`, `for<F: Field<T>>` bounds, `fn_info`), and 2b adds `dyn` and fn-pointer calls in const checked at evaluation and `const static { .. }` blocks that run any code at compile time; phase 3 builds types from const code (`type_of!`).
- [v2/plan/bounds.md](v2/plan/bounds.md) (2026-11-09): Every speed-of-light bound blaze is held to, one machine-read block each; harness/v2/bounds.py reads this file and budgets.py measures it.
- [v2/plan.md](v2/plan.md) (2026-11-09): The plan for blaze, whole, on one page. The goal, the rules, the one design every part shares, the targets, and how the work is run; the ledger of objectives is plan/objectives.md.
- [memory-footprint.md](memory-footprint.md) (2026-11-09): Why a stage5 self-build's daemon reached 75.7 GiB against a 47 GiB limit on the Mac (freed memory pinned by long-lived blocks on the same heap, query storage that only grows, two measures of memory), and the fix: an owner per lifetime (frames reset per item, outputs as records in the store's own vmcache-style buffer pool), footprint as the one measure, telemetry first.
- [v2/plan/design/named-locks.md](v2/plan/design/named-locks.md) (2026-11-05): Every lock in blaze is a named blaze_core::lock::{Lock, ReadLock, Signal} that records who waited, behind whom and for how long, on the slow path only; raw std and parking_lot locks are banned; the profile ranks locks by wait time (`lock_waits`, `blaze debug locks`) and the gate fails a build where one lock eats a share of worker time.
- [v2/plan/design/explore-generic.md](v2/plan/design/explore-generic.md) (2026-11-05): The explorer for any program that emits blaze telemetry, not just the blaze daemon. ix-prof gains the one serving side (feature `explore`, the WebTransport server, certificate, link, token and live stream moved out of blaze-explore) behind a `Source` trait; the protocol speaks of generic things (processes, threads, open spans, tasks with state, progress and a "waiting on", task edges); build steps, crates and build scripts are the `blaze` layer on top, and the daemon is one `Source`. Covers the tables, versions and the gate that keeps ix.dev/explore from falling behind, the page's Running now and Graph views, and the order of the work.
- [v2/plan/design/explore-core.md](v2/plan/design/explore-core.md) (2026-11-05): The explorer's core moves to Rust compiled to wasm32 by blaze (`blaze-explore-core`), the crate the daemon, the build's live view and `blaze status` already share (`blaze_protocol::now`) plus the wire decoding and the trace's aggregation and layout; the page (indexable-inc/ix) keeps only the shell. The producer serves its own core over the session, so page and producer can never disagree on a schema. Each view is written from a question a person asks (is it stuck, what is slow, why did this rerun, where is X and what does it wait on), not from the tables a producer happens to have.
- [v2/plan/design/build-view.md](v2/plan/design/build-view.md) (2026-11-05): The live view of `blaze build`, `check` and `test`, redesigned. One typed model of a build as it runs now (`blaze_protocol::now::Now`: its phase, the daemon's memory against its ceiling and how pressed it is, busy and idle workers with their innermost spans, what the rest waits on and what each blocker holds back, downloads, the slowest so far, how long nothing moved), folded by one sans-IO core from the plane's graph records, the threads' open spans and the downloads, and read by the build's own client, `blaze status` and the explorer's daemon source. Drawn by one sans-IO renderer (`blaze_ui::board`) full screen on a terminal, as a few lines inline, or as a line every few seconds off one; snapshot-tested.
- [memory-pool.md](memory-pool.md) (2026-11-05): The long-term memory design. One budget per machine, run like a database buffer pool. Every byte is charged to a task's frame or to a named cache. Admission uses measured peaks by kind and input size. Every cache is an evictable hot tier over the content-addressed store, with one evictor. Nothing is buffered without a bound. One daemon per machine, and the kernel's limit as the backstop.
- [memory-budget.md](memory-budget.md) (2026-11-05): Memory as a scheduled budget: blaze reads the machine's real limit, admits work by its measured peak, sheds caches under pressure and stops with an error naming what cannot fit, never swapping a machine to death.
- [v2/plan/design/vfs-sync.md](v2/plan/design/vfs-sync.md) (2026-11-04): blaze v2 vfs - the team's source of truth lives on Cloudflare (a Rust Worker built by blaze, run as wasm, a Durable Object per head); multiplayer edits and merges are operations on the syntax tree, not text; jj-style changes with stable IDs, first-class conflicts and an operation log; a branch can stack on another and takes its updates automatically; Pando-style per-head ordering for thousands of agents; blaze builds straight from a synced head; git is only a mirror.
- [v2/plan/design/structured-output.md](v2/plan/design/structured-output.md) (2026-11-04): "Everything blaze says to a person or an agent becomes data first: a `Report` (headline, rule, facts, fixes, blocks, causes) in one crate, `blaze-report`, carried by the daemon's API as CBOR and drawn by one pure renderer as styled text, plain text or JSON; the rendering rules, the build-script `cargo:blaze-report=` directive, `blaze explain`, terminal capabilities and the `[terminal]` config, the progress and summary design for the next slice, and the inventory of what is left to port (2026-11-04, lane structured-output: errors through `ApiError`, the build-script failure, the llvm-sys pin and the sandbox's directive refusal are ported)."
- [v2/plan/design/no-tracing.md](v2/plan/design/no-tracing.md) (2026-11-04): blaze drops the `tracing` crate. Every span and event goes through blaze's own recorder in a new leaf crate `blaze-trace`: one registry for span and event kinds, `span!` and `event!` macros with static call sites, words written straight into the flight ring (no dispatcher, no visitor). The doc gives the grammar, the slot-reuse ordering, the cost budget with its instruction-count bench on the Linux bench runners, the mapping from each tracing form, vendor patch series for third-party crates, a lockfile ban in `blaze check`, and the lanes parallel agents take.
- [v2/plan/design/name-free-identity.md](v2/plan/design/name-free-identity.md) (2026-11-04): Unison-style identities for blaze. A compiled body's store key holds what it does, never what it or its callees are called or where they are written. A name or place is keyed only by code that reads it. Positions are held by table and filled per instance, and the link keeps per-body identity.
- [v2/plan/design/multiconfig-check.md](v2/plan/design/multiconfig-check.md) (2026-11-04): "One `blaze check` over every configuration of a package at once (its targets, feature sets and platforms), and the reachability lints that gives: `blaze::dead` (no configuration uses the item; rustc's `dead_code` over all of them), `blaze::test_only` (only the tests do; `--fix` adds `#[cfg(test)]`) and `blaze::cfg_only` (only some features or platforms do; the narrowest exact `#[cfg]`). Slice 1 is built (2026-11-04, lane multiconfig-check: the host's targets under the features asked for, the three lints, the `#[cfg]` fix with a soundness check); multi-platform and feature-set configurations, tagging every diagnostic with its configurations, and dependency findings are designed here and left."
- [v2/plan/design/lock-policy.md](v2/plan/design/lock-policy.md) (2026-11-04): lock policy (lane lock-policy, 2026-11-04, approved by Andrew) - CI refuses any change to the lock files, naming each move, why and the fix; locally a build writes them but never silently; `blaze.lock` beside `Cargo.lock` pins the blaze release and its nightly, the index's newest publish time and every pinned native input's digests; `lock = required` refuses locally too and blaze's tree sets it; what is built and what is left.
- [v2/plan/design/http3-sans-io.md](v2/plan/design/http3-sans-io.md) (2026-11-04): blaze's QUIC and WebTransport stack becomes sans-IO cores with thin drivers, on rustls. quinn-proto stays as the QUIC core; a new HTTP/3 + WebTransport core in blaze-http (static-only QPACK, SETTINGS, extended CONNECT, WebTransport streams and datagrams) drives it; one tokio driver owns the UDP socket and the timers behind the same driver contract as HTTP/1. quinn, quinn-udp, wtransport and wtransport-proto leave the graph. Covers what blaze uses QUIC for, the contracts, the browser's requirements, the losing designs, migration and tests.
- [v2/plan/design/formal-verification.md](v2/plan/design/formal-verification.md) (2026-11-04): The long-term verifier: blaze translates its own borrow-checked MIR to Lean 4 (a query in the front end) and proves specs written once in blaze's extensions. v0 safe Rust by functional translation, v1 unsafe and interior mutability in an Iris-style logic, v2 atomics (SC, then RC11), v3 crashes on files and mmap (Perennial-style, sharing the DST's kernel model), v4 compiler correctness. DST stays on everything.
- [v2/plan/design/deadline-waits.md](v2/plan/design/deadline-waits.md) (2026-11-04): Every blocking kernel wait goes through one blaze-core primitive that takes an absolute deadline on the injected clock and recomputes the time left on every retry; the profile sampler stops interrupting threads with signals; a stuck daemon start names the span it is stuck in.
- [profiling.md](profiling.md) (2026-11-04): blaze's one profiler (lane observe; a plan until each part it describes lands), one span stream into one buffer with several readers. The schema (spans, counters, builds, processes, test_runs, samples, images, provenance, inputs, alloc_samples, heap_by_owner, panics; Arrow, defined once in crates/blaze-profile/src/schema.rs), the flight recorder, the Parquet history with `blaze debug sql` and `nix run .#duckdb`, the client's rows in it, the live feed (`blaze debug live`, the explorer), the stall watchdog, and `BLAZE_PROFILE` as an export from the history.
- [v2/plan/design/why.md](v2/plan/design/why.md) (2026-11-02): blaze why, which says exactly why the last build computed something again instead of reusing it, by key part, read or reason, never by guess.
- [v2/plan/design/verus.md](v2/plan/design/verus.md) (2026-11-02): Formal verification in blaze by forking Verus. Verus's syntax is native blaze grammar, gated per crate by `#![feature(blaze_verify)]` and lowered in hir-def. crates/hir-ty-verus lowers blaze's HIR into Verus's VIR (replacing rust_verify, rule by rule), and vendored vir and air prove it with a pinned, seeded, resource-limited Z3. Each function's proof is a kernel step keyed by its VIR, and `blaze check --verify` runs it. Stage 2 sizes rustc_public on blaze's MIR, so Kani can run.
- [v2/plan/design/verify.md](v2/plan/design/verify.md) (2026-11-02): How blaze checks its own store and incremental builds: BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE recomputes a sampled fraction of store hits and compares bytes, and a Hegel edit fuzzer holds every incremental build to a clean one through the invalidation oracle (blaze-v2-proof).
- [v2/plan/design/vecreport.md](v2/plan/design/vecreport.md) (2026-11-02): Lint `blaze::vecreport` - report what LLVM's optimized code still does in a loop (a bounds, overflow or panic check that survived, a loop left scalar and why) at the source line, read from the IR after every pass and the loop vectorizer's remarks, hot loops only under a profile; prior art, the design, the guarantee it rests on, and what the stencil tier can say.
- [v2/plan/design/toolchain-c.md](v2/plan/design/toolchain-c.md) (2026-11-02): blaze uses only its own pinned LLVM and ships one pinned C toolchain built from it (clang, lld, compiler-rt, libc++, wasi-libc, libc stubs), so no compiler, sysroot, SDK or runtime the machine installed changes what blaze builds; rustup and the nightly download go.
- [v2/plan/design/tail-calls.md](v2/plan/design/tail-calls.md) (2026-11-02): lane tailcall: `become` (explicit_tail_calls) as a guaranteed tail call through the front end, the MIR evaluator, the stencils and LLVM; dev code is stencils, which make one, and wasm refuses it by name.
- [v2/plan/design/storemodel.md](v2/plan/design/storemodel.md) (2026-11-02): lane storemodel's model checker of the store and kernel protocol (crate blaze-storemodel): the real blaze-cas Store, Writers and Kernel driven through every schedule of a few actors, a crash after every IO step on a file system that models what a crash keeps, and a restore checked against six properties.
- [v2/plan/design/specialization.md](v2/plan/design/specialization.md) (2026-11-02): Sound specialization as an opt-in blaze extension, `#![blaze::specialization]` with `#[blaze::specialization_trait]`, built on rustc's always-applicable rule (min_specialization) without its unsafe markers; rustc's min_specialization checks are ported for std and the crates that enable the feature.
- [v2/plan/design/sealed-orphan.md](v2/plan/design/sealed-orphan.md) (2026-11-02): Relaxing the orphan rule soundly as an opt-in blaze extension: `#[blaze::sealed]` traits whose crate may write `impl<T: Sealed> ForeignTrait for T` (built, with its checks in `hir-ty-coherence`), and the ranked alternatives, including a whole-workspace coherence domain (designed, not built).
- [v2/plan/design/scheduler.md](v2/plan/design/scheduler.md) (2026-11-02): Why the scheduler, not the thread pool, was the bottleneck in blaze v2 builds (barriers hiding work, unit costs of 1), and the plan that replaces it: real plane costs, write-once slots, per-crate maintainer nodes, name resolution per crate.
- [v2/plan/design/pure-fns.md](v2/plan/design/pure-fns.md) (2026-11-02): "#[blaze::pure] and #[blaze::pure(trusted = ..)]: functions that read the world only through their arguments, checked transitively over MIR; what counts as observing an address, which std calls are allowed, and the memory and purity facts every function gets."
- [v2/plan/design/polymorph.md](v2/plan/design/polymorph.md) (2026-11-02): Polymorphization in blaze v2 (lane polymorph, 2026-11-02) - one copy of a generic instance for every set of type arguments its code can't tell apart (unused, used only by size and alignment, used only through a table), decided by the share key before codegen; ADT facts become structural shapes, codegen-answered calls are keyed by full identity, what rustc's polymorphization did and why it was removed, the guarantee relied on, the dictionary-passing design left for later, and how it is measured.
- [v2/plan/design/perf-history.md](v2/plan/design/perf-history.md) (2026-11-02): Performance history of the programs blaze builds (lane perf-history). Each profiled run is one row set in the profile history (the run with its exact tree, blaze, binary and host; per function self and total samples, by path and by code identity), and `blaze perf diff <run> [<base>]` gives per function the change in time with a noise bound and the cause class read from the identities (its code changed, built with other settings, a callee changed, or same code and callees). Built: the code map each link writes, the rows and their Parquet round trip, the identity join, the diff (text and JSON) and `blaze perf record|runs|diff`. Designed: the `--prof` switch that records on its own, call and instruction counts.
- [v2/plan/design/lint-borrow-workarounds.md](v2/plan/design/lint-borrow-workarounds.md) (2026-11-02): blaze's `blaze::borrow_workaround` and `blaze::nll_workaround` — code written around a weaker borrow checker than blaze's (a second lookup, a clone to end a borrow, an index loop for a cursor, take and put back), found only when the direct form passes blaze's checker on the rewritten MIR and behaves the same; what is built (the double lookup), how a rewrite is checked, how published crates are kept building on stable Rust, and the shapes still to build.
- [v2/plan/design/linear.md](v2/plan/design/linear.md) (2026-11-02): "#[blaze::linear]: a type whose values may not be dropped implicitly, checked on built MIR with the borrow check; generic code admits one only through a `#[blaze::linear]` type parameter."
- [v2/plan/design/kernel.md](v2/plan/design/kernel.md) (2026-11-02): blaze v2's kernel: registered pure compute steps from MIR down, each value kept in the store under its identity, its step's code and flags, with the narrow reads it made and their hashes, verified on lookup; codegen's dev templates are its first entries.
- [v2/plan/design/icf.md](v2/plan/design/icf.md) (2026-11-02): Identical code folding in blaze v2 (lane icf, 2026-11-02) - equal instances are one before codegen (the share key) and one after it (dedupe by code ID, relocations by what they name, to a bounded fixpoint), the linker given one copy with every relocation renamed to it, statics included; what never folds, the guarantee relied on, and how it is measured.
- [v2/plan/design/heap-to-stack.md](v2/plan/design/heap-to-stack.md) (2026-11-02): HeapToStack, blaze's own MIR pass: a Box::new, Rc::new or small vec! whose allocation never leaves its function lives in the function's frame instead, only in programs whose allocator is std's, capped per value and per frame, and never in a frame that can recur.
- [v2/plan/design/field-order.md](v2/plan/design/field-order.md) (2026-11-02): Field order by heat (lane fieldorder, 2026-11-02) - the fields a profile shows hot code reading laid out first in `repr(Rust)` structs and enum variants, only when the type keeps rustc's size, alignment, ABI, niche and tag; the Reference text that allows it, what is never reordered, the heat estimate from built MIR weighted by PGO counts, the plan input and its place in layout identity, the tests, the benchmark, and the driver hook still to add.
- [v2/plan/design/effects.md](v2/plan/design/effects.md) (2026-11-02): "#[blaze::nopanic], #[blaze::noalloc] and #[blaze::nonblocking]: effects checked over MIR on pure's walk, and where #[blaze::constant_time] would sit."
- [v2/plan/design/doctests.md](v2/plan/design/doctests.md) (2026-11-02): "Doctests built and run by blaze with its own front end, never rustdoc: rustdoc's rules for finding examples, writing their programs (line-aligned to the docs) and judging them, ported; each example is its own unit (its own crate, binary and process, patched on an edit like any blaze test), never merged, in any edition; what is built (2026-11-02, lanes doctest to doctest5: `blaze test --doc` builds each example as its own crate in parallel, builds and links only an edited one while every other is found unchanged by one store lookup, builds `test_harness` examples as tests, and runs each in its own process) and what is left."
- [v2/plan/design/devirt.md](v2/plan/design/devirt.md) (2026-11-02): Whole-program devirtualization. A final binary's walk lists every vtable the program makes, and the program's facts are closed per object type. A MIR pass then turns `dyn` calls into direct calls (one type) or vtable compares (two to four), keyed by the facts each body read. A second walk lists the new direct callees. Covers what makes a set closed, the guarantees relied on, vtable identity, and the PGO producer still to build.
- [v2/plan/design/contracts.md](v2/plan/design/contracts.md) (2026-11-02): Function contracts (nightly's `#![feature(contracts)]`) in blaze — the same as the pinned nightly first, then checked by default in dev and test profiles, tested by Hegel-generated property tests, proved by lane verus (`#[blaze::verify]`), and used by the optimizer only once proved.
- [v2/plan/design/constspec.md](v2/plan/design/constspec.md) (2026-11-02): Specializing functions on constant arguments (lane constspec, 2026-11-02) - a MIR pass that lists the calls passing a constant their callee branches on, and a copy of the callee compiled knowing it with the decided branches gone, which the code generator calls; when a call gets one, the budgets that bound the program's copies, why `#[inline(never)]` callees get copies and addressed or exported ones do not, the keys, the guarantees relied on, and the benchmark.
- [v2/plan/design/code-layout.md](v2/plan/design/code-layout.md) (2026-11-02): Profile-guided code layout in blaze's own linker: C3 function order from an ix-prof sampling profile mapped back through per-build address maps, cold functions inferred without a profile and placed last, cold blocks weighted unlikely; hot/cold splitting designed, not built; the benchmark.
- [v2/plan/design/code-identity.md](v2/plan/design/code-identity.md) (2026-11-02): The one definition of code identity in blaze (crates/hir-ty-identity). Compile identity is what one instance's generated code depends on; behaviour identity (CodeId) is what running it can depend on. Both are Merkle graphs with recursion hashed as one strongly connected component. Every other hash of code ports onto them and is deleted.
- [v2/plan/design/clone-out.md](v2/plan/design/clone-out.md) (2026-11-02): Lane clone-out: a second checkout's build directory costs only its own bytes, because every output of 16 KiB or more is a clone of the store's read-only copy, and each build reports the bytes it cloned, wrote and copied.
- [v2/plan/design/borrowck-cursor.md](v2/plan/design/borrowck-cursor.md) (2026-11-02): BLAZE_BORROWCK=polonius-flow, a borrow-check mode that accepts what datalog Polonius accepts and the alpha rejects (linked-list cursors, flow-sensitive invariance), and never less than the alpha.
- [v2/plan/design/bits.md](v2/plan/design/bits.md) (2026-11-02): `#[blaze::bits]`: Zig-style bit-packed structs with ordinary field syntax. Layout is the backing integer's; a field's width comes from its type; field places stay places through borrow checking and are lowered to integer ops by one MIR pass at the end of the runtime passes, so neither the interpreter nor the code generator sees a new projection.
- [v2/plan/design/arbitrary-ints.md](v2/plan/design/arbitrary-ints.md) (2026-11-02): Integers of any width, `u1`..`u128` and `i1`..`i128`, as Zig has them, behind the crate attribute `#![blaze::arbitrary_ints]`. They are real primitive types, shadowed like `u8`. They are stored in the smallest power-of-two container with the unused high bits as a niche, overflow at their width, and get their trait impls from blanket impls in core over a solver-builtin marker trait.
- [ix-prof-format.md](ix-prof-format.md) (2026-11-02): The ix-prof profile format and interfaces. Covers the .ixprof container (canonical JSON manifest, Arrow IPC tables, blake3 id), the tables, symbols, pprof and Chrome exports, the /debug/pprof endpoints, the live stream with cursors, gaps and drop counts, and the design for profiling any blaze-built program with no code changes.
- [future/gpu/raytracing.md](future/gpu/raytracing.md) (2026-11-02): Ray tracing in blaze GPU kernels, built on inline ray query, typed pipeline payloads and acceleration structures that carry lifetimes.
- [future/gpu/plan.md](future/gpu/plan.md) (2026-11-02): Rust kernels in the same crate as the host code, compiled by blaze for Metal, Vulkan, CUDA and the CPU, launched through one typed API.
- [future/gpu/README.md](future/gpu/README.md) (2026-11-02): Index of the plans for compiling Rust kernels to GPUs with blaze.
- [future/bootstrap.md](future/bootstrap.md) (2026-11-02): Bootstrap blaze from a wasm seed (blaze's own source plus blaze compiled to core WebAssembly), so blaze is built only by its seed and by blaze, never rustc or cargo, and its source may use blaze-only Rust.
- [future/autodiff.md](future/autodiff.md) (2026-11-02): Differentiation in blaze on CPU and GPU, from automatic differentiation on MIR, to symbolic derivatives of pure functions, to e-graph simplification shared by both.
- [v2/plan/design/store.md](v2/plan/design/store.md) (2026-11-01): blaze v2: the store.
- [v2/plan/design/proc-macros.md](v2/plan/design/proc-macros.md) (2026-11-01): How blaze v2 expands proc macros (a wasm32-wasip1 module under Wasmtime behind the proc_macro bridge, the MIR evaluator as its reference), keys and keeps the expansions, and what it does to be the fastest.
- [v2/plan/design/profile-history.md](v2/plan/design/profile-history.md) (2026-10-31): lane observe, step 3: the flight recorder's Parquet history, its errors table and `blaze debug diff` (crates/blaze-profile/src/history.rs), the DuckDB views and named queries over it (sql/views.sql, sql/examples.sql, src/views.rs), `blaze debug sql` running the pinned DuckDB CLI (src/sql.rs), and the flush's speed of light.
- [v2/plan/design/may-suspend.md](v2/plan/design/may-suspend.md) (2026-10-31): lane may-suspend (2026-10-31): blaze rejects a value held across a call that may park a fiber when that value must not cross threads (`!Send`, or `#[must_not_suspend]`); may-suspend is inferred from the monomorphized call graph from corosensei's `Yielder::suspend`, written only as `#[blaze::may_suspend]` on a trait method or fn-pointer field. Crate `hir-ty-suspend`; replaces sched phase 2's hand audit.
- [v2/plan/design/fibers.md](v2/plan/design/fibers.md) (2026-10-31): lane sched (2026-10-31): a waiting job never blocks its thread, and the scheduler is a sans-IO state machine. Phase 1 is the synchronous core in crates/blaze-graph/src/sched/ with its property tests (written); phase 2 is stackful fibers (corosensei, decided 18:29): the driver and the query-wait hook are written, the pump's replacement and the thread-local audit follow.
- [v2/plan/design/explore.md](v2/plan/design/explore.md) (2026-10-31): the explorer's daemon side (crate blaze-explore), one source of the general profile explorer beside ixprof files and live programs: an HTTP/3 WebTransport server on 127.0.0.1 that https://ix.dev/explore connects to pinning a 13-day self-signed P-256 certificate by hash; the link, origin and token rules, certificate rotation, the ops and the live stream, the WebTransport probe, and the speed of light of live and tiles.
- [v2/plan/design/item-hash.md](v2/plan/design/item-hash.md) (2026-10-30): blaze v2's item identities: a body's type check, MIR and borrow check are filed in the store under an a-priori hash of everything they read (its own name-resolved HIR with no spans, the signature hashes of what it names, the crate's inputs) plus a constructive trace of the global facts they read (impl sets, method candidates, field names, constant values), so a result is a store read with no deep verify, shared across branches, machines and reverted edits; the hash is anonymous (Unison-style), with names and positions in a presentation layer, locations as a per-crate data table, debug info off the edit path, and item IDs in blaze's own reports.
- [v2/plan/design/dbsp.md](v2/plan/design/dbsp.md) (2026-10-30): Push-based incremental name resolution, impl tables and trait candidate sets (lane dbsp). The relations are views maintained on the write side by deltas, DBSP-style, and published as salsa inputs, one per slice, so an edit costs work proportional to the facts it changes and a reader sees a change only when its slice changed.
- [v2/plan/design/caching.md](v2/plan/design/caching.md) (2026-10-30): blaze v2's cache keys name content and relative layout only, never where a checkout, home, target directory, registry or toolchain is; every layer (toolchain, load, macro expansions, build scripts, codegen, the link manifest) is looked up before the work it saves, and a hit is what a rebuild would make.
- [v2/plan/design/vfs.md](v2/plan/design/vfs.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 vfs lane's design: the Merkle tree, heads and views, rebase, the journal with group commit, recovery and compaction, and the disk watcher as one input of transactions.
- [v2/plan/design/unsafe.md](v2/plan/design/unsafe.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: unsafe where it makes code measurably faster, safe Rust everywhere else, and every unsafe line proved sound by our own tools (a Miri of our own, sanitizers in our code generator, model checking).
- [v2/plan/design/restore.md](v2/plan/design/restore.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the daemon restores from disk instantly: a mapped image with no deserializing, IDs stable across restarts, changed files known from the OS's journal, and work paged in on demand.
- [v2/plan/design/model-checker.md](v2/plan/design/model-checker.md) (2026-10-29): lane safety's model checker for lock-free code (crate blaze-check): shim atomics, locks and threads as coroutines on one OS thread, loom's bounded DPOR over interleavings, every value a load may read under C11, and a model test per lock-free structure against a sequential model.
- [v2/plan/design/memory.md](v2/plan/design/memory.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 manages memory like a game engine: allocators by lifetime (frame, request, view, image), virtual-memory-reserved arenas with stable addresses, pools, generational handles, per-subsystem budgets, and zero general-purpose allocations in the warm loop.
- [v2/plan/design/frontend.md](v2/plan/design/frontend.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: what rust-analyzer's front end got wrong for a compiler, and what v2 does instead: incremental name resolution, indexed impls, one token format, signature-only dependencies, mapped files, no IDE-only work.
- [v2/plan/design/data.md](v2/plan/design/data.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: data-oriented layout and compression in every stage.
- [v2/plan/design/concurrency.md](v2/plan/design/concurrency.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: how threads share data: reads never lock or write shared memory, values are immutable once published, task boundaries reclaim memory, no build lock.
- [v2/plan/design/compile-time.md](v2/plan/design/compile-time.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the bigger changes for the fastest compile times: reachability-only codegen, a persistent trait cache, the nightly's own solver, proc macros on our own compiler, tiered compilation and idle cores always working, lazy per-function compilation, copy-and-patch codegen, no link and no rewrite for dev runs, one global cache, semantic edits and declared intent, shared generic code, exact test selection, hash-consing, premapped dependencies, scheduling from history, PGO and BOLT.
- [v2/plan/design/codegen.md](v2/plan/design/codegen.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 codegen lane's design: per-function units, instance keys, templates (the back-end memo up to callee renaming), code dedupe, folding by constants, settings and tiering, release summaries and imports.
- [future/const-macros.md](future/const-macros.md) (2026-10-28): Const macros: proc macros written inline as const fn, run by the const evaluator. Stage 0 is experimental.
- [remote-cache.md](remote-cache.md) (2026-10-27): One shared remote cache for CI and everyone: the gateway, the CAS API, and the slices built and to come.
- [no-rustc.md](no-rustc.md) (2026-10-22): The no-rustc rule and the plan to remove every rustc use, step by step, with what is done.

## Records

Research, reports and measurements, true on their date and not brought up to date. Newest first.

- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) (2026-11-03): Changelog: every user-visible change, by release, with [Unreleased] on top.
- [support.md](support.md) (2026-10-30): What blaze v1 supported, cell by cell, each pointing at the report or harness run behind it. v2 has none of these measurements yet.
- [platforms.md](platforms.md) (2026-10-30): The state of each platform under blaze v1 (rustc's link line, the splice, `blaze-engine weaken`), from v1's last CI run that covered them all. v2 has not been run on any platform yet.
- [fn-cache.md](fn-cache.md) (2026-10-30): #[blaze::cache]: results of pure functions kept across runs, keyed by the code they reach. Its library crates were deleted on 2026-10-30.
- [doc.md](doc.md) (2026-10-30): blaze doc as blaze v1 did it (the engine's doc.rs, over a workspace loaded into rust-analyzer): HTML documentation written from the front end's HIR, with no rustdoc. v2 has no `blaze doc` yet.
- [rename.md](rename.md) (2026-10-28): The rename from ra-jit and cargo blaze to blaze (#270), and what tools/rename.py changes.
- [results.md](results.md) (2026-10-27): Results: every number with the harness, commit and report it came from.
- [flat-syntax.md](flat-syntax.md) (2026-10-22): Flat syntax trees for files nobody edits (#42): the design and its memory and time, measured.
